rows.citation: Kumbhar P., Awile O., Keegan L., et al. (2020). An Optimizing Multi-platform Source-to-source Compiler Framework for the NEURON MODeling Language. Computational Science - ICCS 2020, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, pp. 45-58.
rows.model_type: NMODL mechanism files (ion channels, synapses) for NEURON/CoreNEURON; source-to-source compiler and code generator, benchmarked on large brain-tissue network simulations
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no fault injection or mutants; transformations are compiler optimization passes (inlining, symbolic simplification, optional Pade approximation of exponentials).
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - evaluation is kernel and whole-simulation performance benchmarking on two production circuit models, not a stimulation battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - retrieved text reports speedups; numerical validation against the original transpiler is only mentioned as enabled, with no feature comparison.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - optimization targets generated-code performance, not the selection of test protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - parser compatibility shown on 6,370 ModelDB channels; no discovery/held-out split of models or faults.
rows.ai_transformations: no - rule-based AST and SymPy transformations, not AI-generated edits.
rows.software: NMODL Framework - https://github.com/BlueBrain/nmodl (GitHub API: Apache-2.0, repository archived)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Produces translations intended to preserve behaviour (NMODL to C++/ISPC, AST optimizations, optionally approximated exponentials); it is not a behavioural test method. NeuroSem would supply the complementary check this paper does not report: multi-protocol current-clamp feature fingerprints with refinement-calibrated tolerances, mutant-calibrated protocol selection and held-out evaluation, at the NeuroML/LEMS level rather than NMODL.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (DOI metadata: title, 7 authors, LNCS / ICCS 2020, pp. 45-58); Semantic Scholar batch API (LNCS abstract; externalIds link PMC7302241 and arXiv 1905.02241); Europe PMC search record PMC7302241; arXiv abs page and arXiv v1 PDF text extracted locally with pypdf (validation, ModelDB and GitHub reference [50] passages); GitHub REST API for BlueBrain/nmodl. Note: arXiv v1 abstract reports ~10x production speedup, LNCS abstract ~7x (version difference, not a metadata conflict).

rows.citation: Viswan N.A., HarshaRani G.V., Stefan M.I., et al. (2018). FindSim: A Framework for Integrating Neuronal Data and Signaling Models. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 12.
rows.model_type: Multiscale neuronal signalling models (biochemical reaction networks, SBML) simulated in MOOSE; framework states it extends to electrophysiology experiments
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - model variants include 'mutant'/disease versions (e.g. loss of a molecular species) scored against experiments; biological variants, not single-fault software mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - structured database of many experiments (time-series, dose-response, multi-stimulus) with defined stimuli, each run against the model.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - states current- and voltage-clamp experiments fit the format, but demonstrated readouts are biochemical signalling outputs, not spike features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - experiment scores can feed model parameter optimization; experiments are not selected or minimized for detection power.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out models, experiments or fault families found in the full text.
rows.software: FindSim - https://github.com/BhallaLab/FindSim (GitHub API reports no detected license); MOOSE simulator
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: FindSim anchors successive model versions to experimental data through a battery of scored experiments, which overlaps with running a test battery across model versions. NeuroSem instead compares a transformed model against its own reference under synthetic current-clamp protocols with eFEL features and refinement-calibrated tolerances, uses controlled single-fault mutants to select a compact protocol set, and evaluates that set on held-out models and a held-out mutation family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (title, 4 authors, Front. Neuroinform. vol 12, 2018); Europe PMC REST search (PMID 29997492, PMC6028806, abstract) and full-text XML keyword scan (experiment categories, scoring, optimization, GitHub link); Semantic Scholar batch API; GitHub REST API for BhallaLab/FindSim.

rows.citation: Farhan M., Krejci C., Olsen M., et al. (2021). Metamorphic Testing for Hybrid Simulation Validation. 2021 Annual Modeling and Simulation Conference (ANNSIM), pp. 1-12.
rows.model_type: Hybrid (agent-based plus discrete-event) simulation model; restaurant server helping-behaviour case study
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear - abstract does not mention mutation analysis or seeded faults; full text paywalled and not read.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - metamorphic relations vary model inputs (index terms mention inter-arrival time, group size, walking speed); not electrical stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - operational simulation outputs; no neuroscience.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - abstract gives no indication of selecting or minimizing a set of metamorphic relations.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Applies metamorphic testing to validate one non-neuroscience hybrid simulation when data are scarce. NeuroSem is differential (transformed versus reference model) rather than relation-based, works on NeuroML neuron models with electrophysiology features, calibrates tolerances by refinement, and adds mutant-calibrated protocol selection with held-out model and fault-family evaluation. Metamorphic testing of simulations per se is not a NeuroSem novelty claim.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (title, 4 authors, ANNSIM 2021, pp. 1-12); IEEE Xplore REST abstract endpoint for document 9552058 (abstract, index terms); Semantic Scholar batch API (abstract, DBLP key conf/annsim/FarhanKOR21). Full text not accessed (paywall).

rows.citation: Ramanathan A., Steed C.A., Pullum L.L. (2012). Verification of Compartmental Epidemiological Models Using Metamorphic Testing, Model Checking and Visual Analytics. 2012 ASE/IEEE International Conference on BioMedical Computing (BioMedCom), pp. 68-73.
rows.model_type: Compartmental epidemiological ODE models (SIR/SEIR-type; birth/death rates, multi-host/pathogen scenarios)
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear - abstract claims the workflow detects implementation errors, but no systematic seeded-fault study is described; full text not read.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - several modelling scenarios and visual parameter scans alongside metamorphic relations; not stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - epidemic dynamics outputs, not neuronal features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection of a compact test or scenario set described.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - initial results on example models; no held-out split.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest in spirit of the metamorphic-testing items here: behavioural verification of ODE biology models combining metamorphic testing with process-algebra model checking and visualization. It does not report mutation-calibrated scoring, multi-protocol feature fingerprints, refinement tolerances, protocol selection or held-out evaluation; NeuroSem would add these for neuron models, but offers no formal model checking.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (title, 3 authors, BioMedCom 2012, pp. 68-73); doi.org redirect to IEEE Xplore document 6516431 and IEEE Xplore REST abstract endpoint (abstract, index terms); OSTI API record 1055106 (ORNL version with near-identical abstract). Full text not accessed.

rows.citation: Tang E., Barr E., Li X., et al. (2010). Perturbing numerical calculations for statistical analysis of floating-point program (in)stability. Proceedings of the 19th International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis (ISSTA '10), pp. 131-142.
rows.model_type: General floating-point scientific software (programs from the literature and the GNU Scientific Library)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - systematic value perturbation (random low-order bits) and expression perturbation (real-equivalent rewrites); aims to expose instability, not seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - perturbs internal computations rather than applying a battery of input protocols.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - value perturbation screens candidates for expression perturbation, but there is no test-set selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - evaluated on example programs and GSL; no held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no - automated perturbations, not AI edits.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Background for separating numerical noise from real change: its expression perturbation resembles NeuroSem's valid-transformation false-positive control. NeuroSem works at model and electrophysiology-feature level, sets tolerances from time-step refinement (h, h/2, h/4) rather than bit-level perturbation, and targets behavioural faults across stimulation protocols rather than floating-point stability.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (title, 4 authors, ISSTA '10, pp. 131-142); ACM Digital Library landing page (full abstract); Unpaywall API (closed access); Semantic Scholar batch API (DBLP key conf/issta/TangBLS10). Full text not accessed; DBLP API blocked by a bot check.

rows.citation: Söderlind G., Wang L. (2006). Evaluating numerical ODE/DAE methods, algorithms and software. Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics, 185, 244-260.
rows.model_type: Numerical ODE/DAE solver software (DASPK, RADAU5) evaluated on test problems
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - controlled modifications to DASPK and RADAU5 (error criteria, norms) compared under ceteris paribus conditions; not fault injection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - a test protocol applied across a variety of test problems; not stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - solver accuracy and performance measures.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - outlines principles of a formal test protocol; no optimization of test sets.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out split described in the abstract.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Methodological background on controlled, protocol-based testing of ODE solver implementations, relevant to NeuroSem's numerical mutation family and refinement-based tolerances. NeuroSem does not study solver design; it treats solver settings as one fault family and tests model behaviour through electrophysiology features.
